before.Abstract: Dense process rewards have proven a more effective alternative to the sparse outcome-level rewards in the inference-time scaling of large language models (LLMs), particularly in tasks requiring complex multi-step reasoning. While dense rewards also offer an appealing choice for the reinforcement learning (RL) of LLMs since their fine-grained rewards have the potential to address some inherent issues of outcome rewards, such as training efficiency and credit assignment, this potential remains largely unrealized. This can be primarily attributed to the challenges of training process reward models (PRMs) online, where collecting high-quality process labels is prohibitively expensive, making them particularly vulnerable to reward hacking. To address these challenges, we propose PRIME (Process Reinforcement through IMplicit rEwards), which enables online PRM updates using only policy rollouts and outcome labels through implict process rewards. PRIME combines well with various advantage functions and forgoes the dedicated reward model training phase that existing approaches require, substantially reducing the development overhead. We demonstrate PRIME’s effectiveness on competitional math and coding. Starting from Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Base, PRIME achieves a 15.1% average improvement across several key reasoning benchmarks over the SFT model. Notably, our resulting model, Eurus-2-7B-PRIME, surpasses Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct on seven reasoning benchmarks with 10% of its training data.1

semanticFindings.valsAggregation: Vals Index, Finance Index and Legal Index aggregate existing component measurements; do not count as independent measurements or infer independent sample size from summed tasks.
semanticFindings.financeFormula: (1.6 * AVG(FinanceAgentV2_1, EMBV1_1) + .5 * TaxAgentBench) / 2.1; standalone component scores; Tax all-pass.
semanticFindings.legalFormula: 0.978 * Lines + 0.022 * TaxAgentBench; Lines revenue-weights eight practice-area components, using available LRB all-pass/HLAB criteria-pass scores, plus Tax weighted pass rate. New 10/23 and recorded in 10/24 report; current 27→28 model addition.
semanticFindings.kimi: All ten overall rows: reasoning_effort=max, compute_effort=null, provider=Moonshot AI, temperature=1, top_p=.95, max_output_tokens=262144. All fallback sources available; 0 fallbacks, 0 refusals; without-fallback scores equal published.
semanticFindings.arc3Metric: Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), mean over 55 semi-private environments, not solve rate.
semanticFindings.arcHarness: Standard carries chosen notes; Provider Adapter preserves opaque reasoning state and compacts conversations. Keep harness identities separate.
semanticFindings.arcCoverage: Sonnet5.5 ProviderAdapter xhigh notes partial dataset coverage, full-catalog denominators, recorded usage only and unrecorded attempts excluded. Actual semi-private attempted count not disclosed.
semanticFindings.arcCostUnits: ARC1/2 costPerTask (USD/task); ARC3 cost total (USD/run). PublicDemo replay count and score.total configurations are not semi-private denominator.
semanticFindings.frontierSWE: 21 entries in all three modes at bare URL, ?check=20261025 and ?v=20261025; same as Oct24. Coverage matrix separately contains a Sonnet5.5 proximus result outside ranking; retain coverage-vs-ranking distinction.
